An insurance service manager wants to prepare an up-to-date review. The team has records of customers, policies and claims.

For each policy with claims, select the one with the latest date. If several share that date, select the largest claim number. Show its claim number, policy number, date, type, claim amount and status. Include all activity statuses and omit policies without activity. Arrange the list by policy number, smallest first.

How would you prepare this information? Explain your approach in your own words. You do not need to write SQL.
solution_approach: I will row number claims partitioned by policy id from newest to oldest by claim date and claim id. I will keep row number 1 as the latest event.
schema: customers(customer_id PK, customer_name, city, segment, joined_date); insurance_products(product_id PK, product_name, category, status, base_value); policies(policy_id PK, customer_id FK, product_id FK, start_date, status, premium_amount); claims(claim_id PK, policy_id FK, claim_date, claim_type, quantity, amount, status)
learner_question: If a policy has multiple claims on its latest claim date, which one should be selected?
manager_reply: Pick the claim with the largest claim number on that latest date, and omit policies without claims.
